clue.text: Topple series of deliveries worth recycling

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler

indicators.note: recycling turns material into something new, so the letters of worth are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket over so good it deserves to be reused, enough to topple the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a cricket term for six balls bowled in a row by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow a ruler or regime is to topple it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: So upset, tolerated British dramatist

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word So is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
borne is the past participle of bear, to put up with

explanation.surface: Someone so upset that they merely put up with a British playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: John Osborne wrote Look Back in Anger.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne was the English playwright behind Look Back in Anger, one of the Angry Young Men.

clue.text: Confine knight in the City a long time

indicators.note: the knight is placed inside the letters for the City

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
N is the chess notation for a knight
an age is a very long period

explanation.surface: A knight shut away in the City of London for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postal district covering the City, the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To encage something is to shut it in a cage, so it means to confine or imprison.

clue.text: Emblem to carry over top of mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: to tote is to carry, especially something heavy

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so only the start of mountain is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An emblem to be carried over the summit of a mountain, like a flag at the peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a sacred object or symbol adopted as an emblem of a clan or group.

clue.text: This Greek character is heard in sequence

indicators.note: the clue asks us to listen, so a word for sequence is turned into one that sounds the same

parts.note: a row is a line or series of things one after another

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like statement that a Greek letter can be heard in some series.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to R.

clue.text: Richard is now shifting item of furniture

indicators.note: the letters are moved around, so the three words Richard is now are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Richard is busy moving a piece of furniture around the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A Windsor chair is a traditional wooden chair with a spindle back, a classic piece of furniture.

clue.text: Foundation established by graduates coming to island

indicators.note: the graduates arrive at the island, so one piece is joined directly to the other

parts.note: BAs are holders of a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A foundation set up by university graduates arriving on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the underlying support or starting point on which something rests.

clue.text: Old market's advertising poster's over entrance

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the old market itself

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: billing is promotion on posters; the 's adds the S
a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: A poster for a famous old market hangs over the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate was London's historic fish market, moved from the City to Docklands in 1982.
explanation.definitionFit: Billingsgate is the name of the old London fish market, famous for its porters' coarse language.

clue.text: A tree was rotting in brine

indicators.note: rotting suggests decay and breakdown, so the letters of A tree was fall apart and reform

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree was decaying while standing in salt water.
explanation.definitionFit: Brine is salty water, and the sea is the most familiar example of it.

clue.text: Male animal found by old character in shrub

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, rabbit or hare
thorn is an Old English letter written as þ, standing for th

explanation.surface: A stag found beside an ancient carved letter, hiding in a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Thorn is a runic letter once used in English for the th sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckthorn is a thorny shrub or small tree of the genus Rhamnus.

clue.text: Some backwards diagonal line, that's plain

indicators.note: the run is read from right to left
only some of the letters are used, a run inside the phrase

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A line drawn backwards on a slant across what is otherwise a flat area.
explanation.walkthrough: Read diagonal line from right to left and the answer sits across the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a grassy treeless plain, especially in northern South America.

clue.text: Miners get retrained as fighting units

indicators.note: retraining reshapes the miners, so the letters of Miners get are given a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Former miners are retrained to form army units.
explanation.definitionFit: Regiments are permanent military units, typically commanded by a colonel.

clue.text: Sanction to fail to get up?

parts.note: not makes a verb negative, so to fail to do something is not to do it
arise means to get up from bed or a seat

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether approving something means staying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To notarise a document is to have a notary certify it, giving it official approval.

clue.text: Uncertain number, number that's lower

parts.note: in mathematics n stands for an unspecified number
read as numb-er, something that numbs; ether is an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A vague figure followed by another figure that is smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: The second number is read as numb-er, a thing that numbs, which ether did as an early anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old word for lower or under, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Duck escapes from two-wheeled vehicle — this duck?

indicators.note: the zero leaves the vehicle, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: a scooter has two wheels
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A duck runs off from a scooter, and it turns out to be a duck itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The first Duck is a cricket score of nothing, the shape of O; the final duck is the real bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoters are dark sea ducks of the genus Melanitta, found in northern waters.

clue.text: Big character in eg Belfast?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a seat of government, as Belfast is for Northern Ireland

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Belfast is an example; it is the capital city of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an upper-case letter and the chief city where a government sits.

clue.text: Enemy destroyed one Arab native

indicators.note: a destroyed enemy is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An enemy has been wiped out by one Arab local.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni is a person from Yemen, an Arab country in the south of the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Hotel in awkward situation with a piano in pile of rubbish

indicators.note: the hotel letter goes inside the word for an awkward situation

parts.note: a scrape is a predicament or tight spot
H is Hotel in the phonetic alphabet
taken as written
p is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A hotel in trouble with an old piano, which is headed for the dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a heap of waste or discarded material, especially scrap metal.

clue.text: Feature outside house with touch I love

parts.note: a pat is a light touch with the hand
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A home's outdoor feature that I love with a personal touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved area next to a house used for sitting outside.

clue.text: One business coming to a holiday island

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
biz is informal shorthand for business, as in showbiz
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company arriving at a resort island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island famed as a destination for holidaymakers and clubbers.

clue.text: A great number intended, we hear, to get plot for growing

indicators.note: the phrase is listened to, so a lot meant becomes a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a lot gives a great number and meant gives intended

explanation.surface: Plenty of people were meant to receive a plot for growing vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an allotment is a small rented plot of land for growing fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a parcel of land rented out by a council for cultivating produce.

clue.text: Garland that is left to be put up

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up raises the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A garland that is left behind, waiting to be hung up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian wreath of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: This chief is a male always

parts.note: taken as written
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A statement that a certain leader will forever be a man.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer, also spelt emir, is a ruler or commander in parts of the Muslim world.

clue.text: Leader adroit with lie unfortunately

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events breaks things up, so the letters of adroit and lie are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political leader skilfully but regrettably tells a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader here is the newspaper sense, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader in British newspapers is the main opinion article, also called an editorial.
